subject.title: [Bug]: Potential resource leak in runBoundTurnWithMissingThreadRecovery -- retry not wrapped in try/finally after thread spawn

question: Should Codex app-server bound conversation threads keep a persistent app-server subscription between inbound turns, or should OpenClaw reattach and unsubscribe per turn?
rationale: Current behavior appears to rely on persistent subscriptions for later bound-turn notifications, while the reported leak would be fixed by cleanup only if reattach or binding-clear semantics are also settled.

options.title: Preserve persistent subscription by default
options.body: Keep current multi-turn delivery semantics and add only targeted cleanup where the binding is cleared or the next turn is guaranteed to reattach.

options.title: Move to per-turn reattach and cleanup
options.body: Change bound turns to explicitly attach before each turn/start and unsubscribe afterward, with consecutive-turn and missing-thread recovery tests.

options.title: Document current retention as intentional
options.body: If the replacement thread should remain subscribed after retry failure for future turns, close the issue after adding a focused test or maintainer note that locks that contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve persistent subscription by default
recommendation.body: Keep current multi-turn delivery semantics and add only targeted cleanup where the binding is cleared or the next turn is guaranteed to reattach.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the best available routing owner from the history because he committed the original recovery change and authored adjacent Codex app-server lifecycle work.
